question: In which of the following state the Amrabad Tiger Reserve is located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Amrabad Tiger Reserve** is located in the state of **Telangana**, India.
 
• It was previously part of the **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve**, which is the largest tiger reserve in India. After the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh in 2014, it became part of Telangana.
 
• The reserve covers a vast area of **2,611 square kilometers** and is known for its lush greenery, deep valleys, and diverse flora and fauna.
 
• The reserve is home to a wide range of wildlife, including **Bengal tigers, leopards, sloth bears, wild dogs, spotted deer, and various bird species**.
 
• The Amrabad Tiger Reserve is also significant for its tribal population, particularly the **Chenchu tribe**, who have lived in harmony with nature for centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Features of Amrabad Tiger Reserve:**

 
 
• The reserve is located in the **Nallamala Hills** and is characterized by rugged terrain, gorges, and plateaus.
 
• It is part of the **Deccan Plateau** and features dry deciduous forests interspersed with grasslands.
 
• It serves as an important watershed area for the **Krishna River**, which flows nearby.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Efforts:**
 
 
• The reserve is managed under the guidelines of **Project Tiger**, a national initiative launched by the Government of India in **1973** to protect tigers and their habitats.
 
• Conservation measures include wildlife monitoring, habitat restoration, and anti-poaching activities.
 
• The involvement of local tribal communities, such as the **Chenchu tribe**, plays a crucial role in sustainable conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Eco-tourism:**
 
 
• The Amrabad Tiger Reserve is a popular destination for eco-tourism, offering activities such as safaris, trekking, and birdwatching.
 
• The reserve is home to attractions like the **Farahabad Viewpoint** and the **Umamaheswaram Temple**.
 
• Efforts are made to promote responsible tourism to minimize human impact on the environment.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna:**
 
 
• The reserve's vegetation includes dry deciduous forests, thorn forests, and bamboo groves.
 
• In addition to tigers, the reserve supports a diverse range of fauna, including **gaur, sambar deer, chinkara, and various reptiles**.
 
• The area is also home to many medicinal plants and herbs, adding to its ecological significance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Project Tiger:**

 
 
• Launched in **1973**, it is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at conserving the tiger population in India.
 
• Amrabad Tiger Reserve is one of the many tiger reserves under this project, which currently covers **53 tiger reserves** across India.
 
 
 
• **State Bifurcation:**
 
 
• The state of Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in **June 2014**, leading to the creation of Telangana.
 
• The Amrabad Tiger Reserve, originally part of the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, was allocated to Telangana.
 
 
 
• **Chenchu Tribe:**
 
 
• The Chenchu tribe is an indigenous community residing in and around the Amrabad Tiger Reserve.
 
• They rely on forest resources for their livelihood and have a deep understanding of the region's biodiversity.
 
• Efforts are being made to integrate their traditional knowledge into modern conservation strategies.
